q: A distributed system is best defined as:
o: One powerful computer with many CPU cores
A collection of independent computers that appears to its users as a single coherent system
A network of computers sharing one physical memory
Any computer connected to the Internet
e: Independent nodes, message passing, one coherent view (slide 16).

q: How do nodes in a distributed system coordinate?
o: Solely by passing messages over a network
Through a shared hard disk only
e: No shared memory and no global clock, so messages are the only way.

q: Which is NOT one of the six core characteristics on slide 17?
e: The characteristic is NO global clock.

q: Scaling 'horizontally' means:
o: Adding more RAM to one server
e: Horizontal = scale out = more machines. Vertical = scale up = bigger machine.

q: A failure in which some nodes fail while others keep running is called:
e: Partial failures are a key challenge (slide 19).

q: In the CAP theorem, 'Availability' means:
o: Every node sees the same data at the same time
Every request gets a response, even if some nodes are down
e: The response may not contain the latest write.

q: During a network partition, a CP system will:
o: Answer every request with possibly stale data
Refuse or delay some requests to keep data consistent
e: It gives up availability to keep consistency.

q: According to the slides, banking systems usually favour:
e: A balance must be the same everywhere; social feeds favour availability.

q: Why is CA rarely a real option for distributed systems?
o: Network partitions will happen, so partition tolerance cannot be given up
CA is the default for all clouds
e: CA only fits a single site with no network split.

q: Which transparency hides that several copies of a resource exist?
e: Replication transparency.

q: In a peer-to-peer architecture:
o: Every node acts as both client and server
Clients never talk to each other
e: Peers are equal; e.g. BitTorrent.

q: A main weakness of the client-server model is:
o: The server is a bottleneck and single point of failure
e: Control and load are centralized at the server.

q: In synchronous (blocking) communication the sender:
e: Asynchronous senders continue immediately.

q: Which failure type includes malicious or arbitrary behaviour?
e: Byzantine (arbitrary) failures are the hardest to tolerate.

q: A response that is correct but arrives too late is a:
e: Timing failure: outside the specified time interval.

q: Replaying a recorded valid message later is called a:
e: Defend with timestamps/nonces and secure channels.

q: In Google's architecture, which component splits huge computations into small parallel tasks?
e: GFS stores data in replicated chunks; MapReduce processes it.

q: In MapReduce word count, the step that groups all (word,1) pairs by word is:
e: Map emits pairs, shuffle groups by key, reduce sums.

q: AWS availability zones exist so that applications can:
o: Survive the loss of an entire facility
e: AZs have independent power, cooling and networking.

q: Openness in a distributed system means:
o: The system uses published, standard interfaces so components can be added or replaced
e: E.g. HTTP, TCP/IP, REST APIs.

q: The final exam for INTE 22253 is:
e: 50% final exam, 2 hours, closed book (slide 3).
